props.title: Goodfellas
props.initialSlug: A mobster's rise, betrayal, and fall in NYC's underworld

sections.content: Goodfellas revolutionized the mob movie genre through Scorsese's kinetic directing style and Ray Liotta's electric performance as Henry Hill. The film's innovative tracking shots, like the Copacabana sequence, influenced countless directors and redefined how to capture criminal glamour on screen. While The Godfather (1972) portrayed the mafia with operatic grandeur, Goodfellas showed the gritty day-to-day reality of mob life - the petty arguments, the constant paranoia, and the brutal violence without romanticization. The film's rapid-fire editing and fourth-wall-breaking narration created a new template for crime cinema.

sections.content: The influence of Goodfellas extends far beyond crime films. Boogie Nights (1997) directly borrowed its style for the porn industry story, while Casino (1995) expanded on its themes in Las Vegas. The film's dark humor and violence inspired Pulp Fiction (1994), with Tarantino acknowledging Scorsese's influence. The rapid editing style and use of popular music became a blueprint for modern filmmaking, evident in works like The Wolf of Wall Street (2013) and American Hustle (2013).

Joe Pesci's portrayal of Tommy DeVito created a new archetype of the volatile gangster, earning him an Oscar and influencing countless subsequent performances. The film's structure - rise, fall, and consequences - became a template for biographical crime films like Blow (2001) and Black Mass (2015). The authentic portrayal of mob life, based on Nicholas Pileggi's book "Wiseguy," set a new standard for crime film realism. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Crime Cinema

sections.content: Contemporary crime dramas continue drawing from Goodfellas' playbook. The Sopranos (1999-2007) creator David Chase cited it as a major influence, while films like The Irishman (2019) deliberately callback to its style. The movie's approach to violence - sudden, shocking, and consequence-heavy - influenced everything from Drive (2011) to Killing Them Softly (2012).
